title: Offramp traffic scripts and heatchecks
content:
Context: personal operative notes for small-surface, conservative off-ramp from v2.3 -> v2.4-p3. Goal is a low-risk gradual traffic extraction strategy for customers on hosted API who opt into the new quantization profile (q4_xm). Using 'offramp' rather than full canary because we want a reversible extraction window and fine-grained cohort controls.

Quick summary of plan:
- Anchor cohorts: pick 4 persistent customer cohorts (A,B,C,D) representing request shapes (short prompts, long chat, high-kv reuse, embeddings-heavy). These are sticky and will be observed continuously.
- Traffic windows: run traffic extraction in micro-bursts (0.1% -> 0.5% -> 1% -> 2%) with hold times: 45m, 60m, 90m, 3h. If all health checks pass we continue; otherwise immediately scale back to previous stable.
- Fallback mapping: route to v2.3 (exact pinned commit) on error/quality regression. Keep model alias mapping in routing service with TTL 30s for fast rollback.

Preflight checklist (manual + automated):
- Infra: confirm node count and reserved capacity for off-ramp cohorts (ticket ENG-4829). Verify autoscaler cooldown 10m, max burst nodes available.
- Routing: double-check alias pin for v2.3 and v2.4-p3; ensure weighted routing config locked by PR (infra PR 1224).
- Observability: confirm dashboards for these metrics are live and tokenized:
  * token throughput (tp/s) by cohort
  * p50/p95/p99 latency end-to-end
  * error-rate (5xx, model-timeout, decode-failure)
  * cost-per-token delta (approx)
  * quality: synthetic eval pass rate on preselected prompt set (see linked eval set id)
  * user-level degrade signal (user-retry rate, retention-suppress)
- Warmup: pre-warm kv caches for long-chat cohorts by sending 5 warmup requests per model shard with typical session lengths. Warmup script path: scripts/warmup/kv_seed.sh (see PR notes).
- Secrets/keys: ensure KMS rotation not scheduled during window.
- Communication: post deployment start ETA in #deployments and tag SRE on first hold breach.

Heatchecks (what to scan during each hold):
- Immediate (first 15m): sudden spike in 5xx or decode failures >0.2% absolute from baseline -> pause and rollback. Check model logs for OOMs and tokenization mismatches.
- Short term (15m-60m): p99 tail > baseline + 250ms OR p95 > baseline + 120ms -> consider scaling pool or reduce batch size. If p99 >= 600ms for >3 consecutive minutes, roll back.
- Quality (rolling): synthetic eval pass rate drop >= 2 percentage points vs baseline across the eval set -> trigger investigation, hold. If user-facing errors or hallucination reports appear in Slack via CS, escalate.
- Resource: GPU memory fragmentation leading to OOMs or repeated instance restarts -> immediate rollback.

Traffic ramp schedule (conservative):
- T0: 0.1% for 45m (anchor cohorts only)
- T1: 0.5% for 60m (anchor + open cohort sampling)
- T2: 1.0% for 90m (broader sample - add embedding-heavy cohort)
- T3: 2.0% for 3h (if all green, schedule A/B expansion next day)
Notes: do not exceed 2% without SRE/ServRuntime approval. Use randomized traffic steering to avoid amplifying a single upstream client.

Rollback/Pin policy (quick reference):
- Soft rollback: shift alias weight back to v2.3 in router (instant) and keep v2.4-p3 for investigation.
- Hard rollback: remove v2.4-p3 from rotation and mark experiment as paused. Collect logs, core dumps, and eval samples.
- Post-rollback: run forensics checklist (collect traces, sampling of failed requests, user request ids), create an incident if user impact >1% of requests during window.

Observability wiring (ad-hoc items to finish):
- Add synthetic prompt set to live eval runner with hourly results exported to dashboard. (TODO: attach eval set id and runner config)
- Create a short-lived alert that calculates relative quality delta vs baseline and notifies #deployments and oncall.
- Perf traces: ensure trace span tags include model-version and quantization flag.

Safety knobs and mitigations:
- Fallback to CPU-only path for non-latency-critical clients if GPU memory becomes constrained.
- Temp limit token caps for off-ramp cohorts to 256 tokens to limit worst-case compute.
- Rate-limiter: enforce soft qps cap per client to avoid thundering during ramp.

Open questions / edge cases to resolve:
- Should we enforce customer opt-in via account feature flag or route by model alias? (Pros/cons: opt-in limits blast radius but requires cohort selection work)
- How to measure subtle quality drift for long-chat conversational clients — metric engineering needed.
- Will quantized kernels change decoding patterns for hyphenated tokens? (Maya to triage with tokenization team)

Quick TODO (diego):
- [ ] Upload warmup script to infra PR and link in routing change set (deadline: 2025-01-18)
- [ ] Add synthetic eval set and hook into dashboard (deadline: 2025-01-20)
- [ ] Schedule SRE window and get approval (deadline: 2025-01-17)
- [ ] Draft customer comms for anchor cohorts (very short blurb: why we route & how to opt-out)

Notes to self: keep the first day conservative. We can iterate faster once warmup and quality signals are rock solid. If we see small regressions that are explainable (e.g., cost drop but small BLEU reduction for embeddings) prefer a staged mitigation (tune quantization params) over immediate full rollback — but only after getting sign-off from product and SRE.

References & quick links:
- PR: infra/pull/1224 (routing pin)
- Ticket: ENG-4829 (capacity reservation)
- Eval runner: confluence page + eval-set-id: eval-2025-offramp-v1
- Slack channel: #deployments (pinned messages include playbook link)

End of log.
